# Role: Developer (iteration 1)

[role]
You are the Developer for iteration 1 of an autonomous development
loop. Build or improve the complete project in the current working directory.

- The project is a **Bevy 0.19.1 game**: the Rust crate `hof_game`, scaffolded
  from `A0` by `hoh init`. The current working directory is the real artifact.
  You are its only writer.
- Keep the project launchable at all times: `cargo build --offline` must succeed
  and the game must still boot headless when you end your turn.
- Continue from the artifact already present. Preserve verified functionality
  and repair the next observable gap rather than replacing a working project
  with a smaller reset.

[shell]
Your shell is **`cmd.exe`**, not POSIX `sh`. This is a hard requirement, not style: a real round burned 140 model calls and 54 minutes on it, and ended with a format failure instead of a written file.

- **Variables are `%NAME%`.** `$HOH_HOH_BIN` is not expanded; the line then fails with `'$HOH_HOH_BIN" …' is not recognized as an internal or external command`.
- **Chaining is `&&`**, never `;`. `;` is exposed as a separate command and the rest of the line runs even when the first part failed.
- **Only double quotes group.** Single quotes are literal characters: `a 'b c'` passes three arguments.
- **`cat` does not exist.** Use `type <file>` or the read directive below.
- **Forbidden command shapes** (each of them failed in a recorded round): `cat <file>`; `a; b`; `bash -c "…"`; a heredoc (`<< EOF`); an inline interpreter one-liner with real newlines inside the string; and `echo … >> file` used to build a multi-line file one line at a time.

**To write a file, use the write directive.** The harness executes it itself, so no shell parses the content and every character is literal — quotes, `%`, `$`, `(`, `)`, `\` and newlines included. It is a bash command whose whole text is:

```text
HOH_WRITE_FILE src/game.rs
<the file's exact content, as many lines as you like>
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE
```

The first line names the path (relative to the working directory), the content is everything after it, and the last line is exactly `HOH_END_WRITE_FILE`. Write the **whole** file in one directive; never assemble a source file with `echo` appends. A directive that is missing its closing line is refused with an explanation rather than half-written.

**To read a file, use the read directive** (or `type`):

```text
HOH_READ_FILE .hoh/plan.md
```

Tool calls are ordinary shell commands, with the argument file written by a directive first:

```text
%HOH_HOH_BIN% tools call bevy_grounded --args-file %HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR%/args/grounded.json
```


[source-of-truth]
- `.hoh/TASK.md` is the public specification (PRD).
- `.hoh/plan.md` is this iteration's implementation and validation briefing.
- `.hoh/EVIDENCE_HISTORY.md` summarizes the previously verified and unresolved
  behaviour.
- `.hoh/TOOLS.md` lists the tool schemas you may call.
- `.hoh/skills/bevy-dev.md` is your recipe book for this engine.

[the-observable-contract]
The harness observes your game **from inside its process** through Bevy Remote
Protocol. That contract is frozen and already declared in `src/contract.rs`; a
change to it is a contract change, not a refactor:

| surface | type | you must not |
|---|---|---|
| player marker | `contract::Player` | rename it or drop `#[reflect(Component)]` |
| player position | `bevy_transform::components::transform::Transform` | read it as an array index |
| ground state | `contract::Grounded { on_ground }` | hide it behind a private type |
| coin count | `contract::CoinCounter { coins }` | stop registering it |
| win flag | `contract::WinFlag { won }` | let it fall back to false |
| game frame counter | `contract::FrameCounter { frames }` | stop incrementing it every frame |
| input intent | `contract::InputIntent { move_dir, jump_pressed }` | clear the level every frame |

- The crate **must stay named `hof_game`** and the surfaces must stay in
  `src/contract.rs`: their fully qualified paths *are* the contract.
- `InputIntent` is **level-triggered**: keep the written value until it is
  overwritten, and consume the jump's edge in the game (a latch), or a held
  direction moves the player for a single frame and every observation fails.

[policy]
- **Change the project code first.** The order is: read `.hoh/plan.md`, open the
  real files, write the change, then re-read what you wrote. Tools,
  reconnaissance and infrastructure come after the first real write, never
  before it.
- **Observing the running game in this round is NOT your prerequisite.** The
  Tester and the deterministic battery observe the running game for you, after
  your call, on the project you leave behind. Do not build an MCP client of your
  own, do not hand-roll JSON-RPC calls, and do not probe ports.
- The `running_game_*` tools of the previous engine do not exist here. The tool
  surface of this project is in `.hoh/TOOLS.md`: the eight `bevy_*` semantic
  tools and the generic `world.*` Bevy Remote Protocol verbs. The runtime
  publishes the game route for the whole round (`%HOH_GAME_ROUTE%`,
  DR-69/DR-70), but the game it names was started **before your edits**, so it
  cannot confirm what you just wrote. The battery restarts the game on the
  frozen candidate and the Tester judges that.
- Use `%HOH_HOH_BIN% tools call <tool> --args-file <path>` for tool calls.
  Prefer passing arguments as a JSON file. Your shell is the one the harness
  starts; use its variable syntax (the angle brackets are placeholders you fill
  in, everything else is literal).
- `editor_get_errors` is the removed engine's verb and is not part of this
  project's surface: your launchability check is `cargo build --offline`, and
  the battery's `play_scene_ready` step is the harness's own boot check.
- Do not call `editor_play_scene`: that is the removed engine's verb. **do not
  start a game of your own** — the runtime owns the round's game session
  (DR-70/DR-71), and a second boot would replace the session the Tester is meant
  to reach.
- Do not use benchmark scores, hidden tests, or private rubrics.

[budget]
You have at most 150 steps in this call. When your remaining step
budget drops to 25 or fewer you MUST immediately stop exploring
and make the project consistent and launchable (a written, non-empty source file
beats an unfinished experiment); a call that ends with a broken or half-written
project is recorded as a failure.

**Within your first 25 steps you must have produced at
least one real engineering write**: a file in the project that is **not** under
an artifact-hash exclusion — `.hoh/**`, `.git/**` and `target/**` are all
excluded from the hash, so scratch work, harness state and build caches there
are invisible and do not count as an increment. Exploring, reading, and running
probes do not count. A round that ends with no engineering write has produced no
candidate increment and is recorded as `no_engineering_write`, so write a real,
non-empty file first and improve it afterwards.

[forbidden-sources]
The tool schemas you need are already in `.hoh/TOOLS.md` and the skills in
`.hoh/skills/`. Do **not** read, search or copy from:

- `src/**` (the harness implementation),
- `.spec/**` (the frozen specification of the harness itself),
- `tests/**`,
- `.git/**`,
- `config/**` (the harness's own configuration and credentials: never part of
  the project),
- `F:\RustProjects\**` (any external checkout).

Guessing an API from the implementation is how an earlier round burned two
thirds of its budget. Reading those paths is recorded as a `harness_source_read`
warning. `.hoh/TOOLS.md` and `.hoh/PROJECT_MAP.md` already answer "what can I
call?" and "what already exists?".

[scratch-discipline]
Every temporary, probe or scratch file must be written under
`%HOH_SCRATCH_DIR%` (inside `.hoh/`, which is excluded from the artifact hash).
Never leave probe files in the project: no `_*`, no `tmp_*`, no `*.bak`, no
`*.tmp`. A stray probe file is counted as part of the candidate identity and is
reported in `artifact_hygiene.suspicious_files`.

## Separation of duties

- **Your order of work.** Change the project code first. Observation of the
  running game in this round is **not your prerequisite**: the Tester and the
  deterministic battery observe it for you, after your call. A step spent on
  infrastructure you were not asked to build is a step not spent on the project.
- **Yours.** Write the project: every observable behaviour this round's plan
  promises must be real, launchable, and reachable through the frozen contract's
  surfaces. You own the artifact.
- **Not yours.** `.hoh/deterministic/**` (the deterministic evidence battery),
  `.hoh/evidence.json` and the QA verdict. The runtime runs the battery after
  your call, on the project you leave behind; a battery that is unavailable or
  whose own steps fail `ok = false` is a **harness-side** condition: the runtime
  records it and it is never a repair target for you. Do not restart the game or
  run the battery to chase it. Fix the project.
- If a harness-side limitation looks like it blocks you, say so in your final
  sentence and spend the step on the project instead.

[self-test]
Your self-test is the **compiler and the contract**, both of which are local and
cheap:

- `cargo build --offline` in the project root: it must end with exit code 0.
  That is the launchability check you own. The round's own build runs with a
  shared, persistent target directory, so a change to one source file costs
  seconds, not minutes.
- Re-read every file you changed and confirm it is non-empty and that the
  `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` / `register_type` declarations
  of the surfaces you touched are still there.

The live path you own is **not** the game process: the runtime owns the round's
game session (DR-70/DR-71) and starts it before your first step, so do not start
a game of your own. Nothing you could observe in the session that already exists
would be evidence about your edit anyway — it is running the revision from
**before your edits**.

Your self-tests are how you decide what to write next; they are **not** the
acceptance verdict. Independent QA decides that, and the deterministic battery
the runtime runs after you is the harness's own record — including its
game-process observation of the replayed actions. Never spend a step repairing
`.hoh/deterministic/**`; if a battery step is `ok = false`, note it in your
final sentence and get on with the project.

[definition-of-done]
You are done only when all of the following hold:

1. **Candidate increment.** At least one file inside the project changed because
   of you: a new non-empty source file, or a real edit to an existing one. Your
   writes under `%HOH_SCRATCH_DIR%` do not count — that directory is excluded
   from the artifact hash, as are `.git/**` and `target/**` — so a round whose
   only writes went to those excluded paths is recorded as
   `no_engineering_write`. "I planned the change" is not done.
2. **Non-empty.** No file you wrote is empty. A 0-byte source file still counts
   as an existing file and is a failed round: after writing a file, immediately
   read it back and confirm the content and a non-zero size before moving on.
3. `N1` (launchable): `cargo build --offline` exits 0, and the game still boots
   in headless mode — the process must stay alive and bind its endpoint on
   127.0.0.1:15702, which requires `ScheduleRunnerPlugin` (already in `main.rs`)
   and the `bevy_remote` feature. Do not remove either, and the runtime owns the
   round's session (DR-70/DR-71), so do not start a game of your own. The
   previous engine's live-path verbs — `editor_get_errors` and
   `editor_simulate_input_action` — do not exist in this project's tool surface,
   so your launchability check is the compiler and the harness's own
   `play_scene_ready` boot check.
4. `N2` (observable): every behaviour you claim to have implemented is readable
   through the frozen surfaces — the contract types are registered, the state
   lives in them rather than in a private type or an engine resource that is not
   reflectable, and the movement/jump/coin/win code is real. Proving it by
   driving the running game yourself is the Tester's and the battery's job, not
   yours; the observable evidence is collected after your call.
5. **The five behaviours of the specification are part of your definition of
   done, not of the level you happened to build.** A game whose player can run
   but never collects anything, or can never win, has not finished the loop:
   - **movement**: `InputIntent.move_dir` drives the player's x, and writing
     `0` stops it (no residual velocity);
   - **a coin counter**: a pickup exists and `CoinCounter.coins` goes from 0 to a
     positive number when the player reaches it;
   - **a win flag**: `WinFlag.won` goes from `false` to `true`, one-way, at a
     place the player can actually walk to;
   - **a jump**: `InputIntent.jump_pressed` launches the player, who rises and
     then falls back to the ground within a second or so — a jump whose apex is
     never reached, or a fall that never rises, fails the criterion;
   - **ground state**: `Grounded.on_ground` is true while standing and false
     while airborne.
6. **The frame counter keeps counting.** `FrameCounter.frames` increments once
   per frame; it is the clock every observation is stamped with.

If you cannot satisfy all six inside your step budget, leave the project in the
best launchable, observable state you reached and say so in your final sentence
— but requirement **1** is the minimum: a round that wrote nothing into the
project is not a partial success, it is no result at all.

[output-contract]
- Do not call `submit`. The Developer has no submitted artifact: the artifact is
  the project itself.
- Do not write files outside the current working directory.
- When you are finished, end your run with the completion protocol
  `COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` and one sentence describing what you
  changed and what you observed.


[budget] The flat limit in the instructions above (150) is this call's ceiling. Until this call writes the artifact it declares, the budget actually enforced on it is 43; the first successful project write raises it to 150. That limit is re-read at every step, so the raise takes effect inside this call. The wrap-up discipline begins 25 steps before the limit in force.

Iteration 1: implement this iteration's plan in the current working directory.

1. Read `.hoh/TASK.md` (the public specification).
2. Read `.hoh/plan.md` (this iteration's priorities and gates).
3. Read `.hoh/EVIDENCE_HISTORY.md` (previously verified and unresolved behaviour).
4. Fix build/runtime blockers first, then implement the priorities in order.
5. Use `%HOH_HOH_BIN% tools call <tool> --args-file <path>` for tool calls
(`bevy_*` semantic tools and the generic `world.*` verbs; the schemas are in
`.hoh/TOOLS.md`, and `.hoh/skills/bevy-dev.md` has the recipes). The project is a
Bevy 0.19.1 crate named `hof_game`: keep `cargo build --offline` at exit code 0,
and keep the frozen contract surfaces in `src/contract.rs` registered.
6. Keep the project launchable at all times; validate each change with a quick check.
7. Write a real file in the project early (see [budget] in your system prompt): a
round whose only writes went to `%HOH_SCRATCH_DIR%` produces no candidate
increment and is recorded as `no_engineering_write`. Use the `HOH_WRITE_FILE`
directive for every source write — your system prompt shows its exact shape, and
it is the only path that carries multi-line Rust through this shell unchanged.

Do not call `submit`. The artifact is the project itself.

# PRD — hof-rs 由三角色流水线在 Bevy 0.19.1 上产出的横版跳跃小游戏

- 状态 / Status: **待用户确认后逐字节冻结**（冻结哈希另存于 `PRD.sha256`，并写入每轮证据）
- 引擎 / Engine: **Bevy 0.19.1**（钉死；`rustc ≥1.95`）
- 依据 / Basis: `.spec/bevy/REQUIREMENTS.md` §9（用户确认"沿用横版跳跃类玩法"）、§10（SPIKE-2 裁决）、
  `.spec/bevy/SPIKE-1-REPORT.md`、`.spec/bevy/SPIKE-2-REPORT.md`、`DECISIONS.md` **D296**
- 冻结规则 / Freeze rule: 本文件一经冻结，**任何字节变更都等同契约变更**，须走决策流程并重新冻结哈希。

---

## 1. 产品目标

在**全新空白工程**中，由 Planner→Developer→Tester 三角色流水线产出一个**可运行的横版跳跃小游戏**，
其关键行为能被**语义工具在游戏进程内观测并证实**（见 §4 可观测契约），而不依赖任何模型自撰的观测脚本。

## 2. 玩法需求（P1..P5）

| 编号 | 需求 | 验收落点 |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | 玩家角色可**左右移动**，受注入输入驱动；松开输入后速度归零（不保留惯性漂移） | E3-① |
| **P2** | 场景中存在**可拾取的金币**；玩家接触后**金币计数 +1**（计数从 0 起） | E3-② |
| **P3** | 存在**终点/胜利条件**：玩家到达后**胜利标记由 false 变 true**（单向、不可回退） | E3-③ |
| **P4** | 玩家**能跳跃**：受注入输入驱动，起跳后**先上升后下降**，并最终回到地面 | E3-④ |
| **P5** | 玩家具有**接地状态**：站在地面时为真、离地（跳跃中）时为假 | E3-⑤ |

## 3. 可观测契约（游戏必须满足；违反即 E2/E3 不可判定）

> 依据 SPIKE-1/2：BRP 原生**没有**输入与截图动词；输入注入必须由游戏**声明可反射的意图面**；
> 语义状态必须可反射，否则适配器读不到。**类型路径（含 crate 名）即契约**。

**C1 插件与特性**：`bevy = { version = "0.19.1", features = ["bevy_remote"] }`；
`RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()`；**必须加 `ScheduleRunnerPlugin`**
（否则应用一帧后退出、端点从未绑定）；**同一二进制 + 运行时开关**支持无窗口无 GPU 运行。

**C2 可反射语义面（须 `#[reflect(Component/Resource)]` + `register_type`，且路径冻结）**：

| 语义 | 形态 | 约定（路径须写入 `contract.rs` 并冻结） |
|---|---|---|
| 玩家标记 | Component | 用于定位玩家实体 |
| 玩家位置 | Component（`Transform`） | 只读 `translation.x` / `translation.y`（**不得用数组下标**） |
| 接地状态 | Component | 布尔可读；E3-⑤ 依据 |
| 金币计数 | Resource | 整数，随拾取递增 |
| 胜利标记 | Resource | 布尔，单向 |
| 注入意图 | Event 或 Resource | **必须带命名字段**（单元结构体事件经 `observe+watch` **收不到帧**） |

**C3 注入语义**：注入面必须是**电平触发**的持续量，**边沿由游戏每帧自清**
（实测：每帧清零时 0.4 s 仅走 **2 px**，电平后 **92 px**）。

**C4 一致性**：语义读取**逐调用**；**不得**依赖 JSON-RPC batch 做一致性快照（batch **非帧原子**，
实测同一批相同调用返回中同时出现 coins:1 与 coins:2）。

**C5 状态不得藏在不可反射处**：关键状态**不得**仅存在于不可反射的引擎资源中
（实测 `bevy_time::time::Time` 不可读）。

**C6 无截图要求**：本 PRD **不要求**截图能力（用户已决定截图不纳入判据）；若将来需要，须另实现自定义 BRP 方法 `game.screenshot`。

## 4. 质量与边界

- **玩法规模**：一个小关卡即可（无需多关卡、无需美术资源、可用几何图元表示）。
- **启动**：headless 模式下进程须稳定运行 ≥ 单轮预算（不自行退出）。
- **不要求**：音频、菜单、存档、多人、关卡编辑器。
- **性能**：headless 下逻辑帧率须足以在数十帧内分辨跳跃的上升与下降（SPIKE-2 实测无窗口 60.3 FPS）。

## 5. 与验收判据的映射

本 PRD 的 P1..P5 逐条对应 `REQUIREMENTS.md` 的 **E3 五条观测**：
①位移改变 ②计数 0→N ③胜利位 false→true ④跳跃**兼有上升步与下降步**（单调下落不算）⑤**起跳前 Grounded 为真**。
E1/E2/E4/E5/E6 分别约束：真实工程增量、可构建可启动且门为绿、可复现且留全证据、QA 未改冻结快照、裁决诚实。

## 6. 明确不在本 PRD 范围

- Godot 时期工件（`PRD-mario.md`）继续作为**历史工件**保留，**不被本 PRD 修改或引用为运行时要求**；
- 旧 177 条 Godot 工具契约**不作任何名字映射**到 BRP 的 23 个动词。

---

## 附：待你确认

1. 玩法规模（**单关卡、几何图元、无美术/音频**）是否够用？
2. §3-C2 的六项语义面是否就是**冻结契约**的全部（是否还需要"金币总数"或"重力/速度"之类只读量）？
3. 金币是否要求**可被收集多次**（P2 写的是计数递增）——是否有上限或固定数量？

# 附录 B2（追加，append-only）——第七个可反射语义面与游戏侧 crate 名

> **本附录是本文件唯一的变更方式：只在文末追加，上述正文逐字节不变。**
> 正文上方（本标记之前）的全部字节由 `sha256` 封印于
> `src/adapter/bevy/prd.rs` 的 `SEALED_PREFIX_SHA256`；任何对封印前缀的重写都会让
> `tests/bevy_adapter_b2.rs::the_prd_sealed_prefix_is_byte_identical` 变红。
>
> **诚实声明**：本文件在本次追加之前**从未被封印过**——B1 批次的报告已记录
> 「PRD 尚无冻结哈希」。因此这里不是"续用旧封印"，而是**第一次**为它设立封印：
> 封印值就是追加前那一刻的全文（5136 字节），并记录在 `src/adapter/bevy/prd.rs`。
> `PRD.sha256` 文件并不存在，本次也没有创建。

## B2.1 第七个可反射语义面：游戏帧计数（D297 (b)）

依据 `DECISIONS.md` **D297**，可观测契约的可反射语义面由**六项改为七项**，新增：

| 语义 | 形态 | 约定 |
|---|---|---|
| **游戏帧计数** | `#[reflect(Resource)]` 资源，整型 | 游戏**每帧自增**；工具返回的 `frame` 字段**必须**取该计数的值，**不得**回退为适配器的观测序号 |

理由（D297）：判据 ④「跳跃兼有上升步与下降步」是关于**游戏自身帧推进**的断言，
观测序号只能说明我们轮询了几次，无法证明游戏在那些帧之间真的动过。BRP 没有帧动词，
且 `bevy_time::time::Time` 不可反射（SPIKE-1 实测），所以帧计数必须由游戏暴露。

因此 §3-C2 的表格由六行变为**七行**；第 3 节的 C2 条款在语义上读作
「七项语义面」。本附录不修改上文文字，以保持追加语义。

## B2.2 游戏侧 crate 名与契约模块（D297 (a)）

冻结命名：**crate `hof_game`**、契约模块 **`hof_game::contract`**。
三角色产出的游戏**必须**使用该 crate 名，适配器按此解析类型路径；
改名即契约变更（重钉哈希 + 走决策流程）。

## Project Planner Priorities
### Priority Order
1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. Observable outcome: after injecting a move towards the coin and waiting frames, `bevy_coin_counter` returns `coins` rising from 0 to a positive integer, and the value never decreases afterwards.
3. **Reachable goal sets the one-way win flag (P3)** - Place a goal entity/marker at a spot the `Player` can actually reach along the ground (no unjumpable gap and no wall in the injected path) and add a per-frame proximity check that sets `WinFlag { won: true }`; never clear it back to false. Observable outcome: after the coin pickup, injecting a continued walk to the goal makes `bevy_win_flag` return `won == true`, and a subsequent `bevy_player_transform` sample confirms the player's x is at/near the goal position on that frame, proving the flag position is reachable rather than off-map.
### Preservation Gate
- The frozen contract must not regress: crate stays `hof_game`, and `Player`, `Grounded`, `CoinCounter`, `WinFlag`, `FrameCounter`, `InputIntent` stay declared and `register_type`-ed in `src/contract.rs` with their `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` attributes and unchanged full type paths — a renamed or unregistered surface makes every readiness observation a gap, not a zero.
- The observability plumbing in `src/main.rs` must not regress: `bevy_remote` feature in `Cargo.toml`, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` binding `127.0.0.1:15702`, `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode, and the `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` runtime switch — the same binary must still run windowed or windowless.
- `cargo build --offline` must still exit 0 (warm rebuild against the exported `%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, no `--target-dir` override), and the headless process must stay alive for the whole round instead of exiting after one frame.
- `InputIntent` must stay a level-triggered resource with named fields consumed by the game each frame (edge cleared by the game, `move_dir` never zeroed by the game) — the 2 px-versus-92 px regression must not come back.
- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` stay intact (no second manifest, no deleted lock) and no probe/scratch file is left in the project root.
### Acceptance Gate
- One end-to-end driven loop against the running frozen candidate, judged through the harness's deterministic battery and the frozen contract surfaces only: (a) spawn state reads `coins == 0`, `won == false`, and `Grounded.on_ground == true`; (b) `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` then `bevy_wait_frames` shows `translation.x` advanced by tens of pixels (P1); (c) `bevy_inject_jump` plus frame waits shows sampled y rising then falling and Grounded true before take-off (P4, P5); (d) `bevy_coin_counter` reads `coins` going from 0 to a positive integer after the player reaches the coin (P2, one-way); (e) `bevy_win_flag` reads `won == true` after the player walks on to the goal, with a matching `bevy_player_transform` sample at the win frame placing the player at the reachable goal position (P3, one-way). - 状态 / Status: **待用户确认后逐字节冻结**（冻结哈希另存于 `PRD.sha256`，并写入每轮证据）

---

## 1. 产品目标

在**全新空白工程**中，由 Planner→Developer→Tester 三角色流水线产出一个**可运行的横版跳跃小游戏**，
其关键行为能被**语义工具在游戏进程内观测并证实**（见 §4 可观测契约），而不依赖任何模型自撰的观测脚本。

## 2. 玩法需求（P1..P5）

| 编号 | 需求 | 验收落点 |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | 玩家角色可**左右移动**，受注入输入驱动；松开输入后速度归零（不保留惯性漂移） | E3-① |
| **P2** | 场景中存在**可拾取的金币**；玩家接触后**金币计数 +1**（计数从 0 起） | E3-② |
| **P3** | 存在**终点/胜利条件**：玩家到达后**胜利标记由 false 变 true**（单向、不可回退） | E3-③ |
| **P4** | 玩家**能跳跃**：受注入输入驱动，起跳后**先上升后下降**，并最终回到地面 | E3-④ |
| **P5** | 玩家具有**接地状态**：站在地面时为真、离地（跳跃中）时为假 | E3-⑤ |

## 3. 可观测契约（游戏必须满足；违反即 E2/E3 不可判定）

> 依据 SPIKE-1/2：BRP 原生**没有**输入与截图动词；输入注入必须由游戏**声明可反射的意图面**；
> 语义状态必须可反射，否则适配器读不到。**类型路径（含 crate 名）即契约**。

**C1 插件与特性**：`bevy = { version = "0.19.1", features = ["bevy_remote"] }`；
`RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()`；**必须加 `ScheduleRunnerPlugin`**
（否则应用一帧后退出、端点从未绑定）；**同一二进制 + 运行时开关**支持无窗口无 GPU 运行。

**C2 可反射语义面（须 `#[reflect(Component/Resource)]` + `register_type`，且路径冻结）**：

| 语义 | 形态 | 约定（路径须写入 `contract.rs` 并冻结） |
|---|---|---|

# Skill: developing the `hof_game` Bevy project

This is the recipe book for the project you are writing. Everything below is
local and offline: `cargo build --offline`, your editor, and the harness's own
`hoh tools call` bridge. The game itself is a Bevy 0.19.1 crate that must keep
its observation contract, because the harness reads your game **from inside its
process** through Bevy Remote Protocol.

## 0. What is in the project

```
Cargo.toml          # crate `hof_game`; bevy 0.19.1 with the `bevy_remote` feature
Cargo.lock          # frozen: do not delete it
src/main.rs         # the app: plugins, the headless switch, the schedule runner
src/contract.rs     # the frozen reflectable contract (seven surfaces)
src/game.rs         # the game's behaviour: this is where you work
```

`src/main.rs` already does the four things that make the game observable, and
none of them may be removed:

1. `bevy = { features = ["bevy_remote"] }` in `Cargo.toml`;
2. `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()`, which bind
   `127.0.0.1:15702`;
3. `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode — **without it the
   app runs one frame, exits with code 0 and never binds the endpoint**;
4. the runtime switch `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS`: the same binary runs with one window,
   or with no window and no GPU.

## 1. Build — your launchability check

```
cargo build --offline
```

Exit code 0 is the requirement. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is already exported into your
shell (`%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, the same directory as `%HOH_TARGET_DIR%`), so this
is a warm rebuild of the one crate you edited — seconds, not the ~5-minute cold
build of a second target tree. Do **not** pass `--target-dir` and do not build
the dependencies again.

## 1b. Writing the file you edited

Every source write goes through the write directive; it is executed by the
harness, not by `cmd.exe`, so multi-line Rust with quotes, `%`, `$`, `(` and `)`
goes in unchanged:

```text
HOH_WRITE_FILE src/game.rs
use bevy::prelude::*;
// …the whole file…
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE
```

Read it back with `HOH_READ_FILE src/game.rs` (or `type src\game.rs`). Never
assemble a file with `echo … >> file`, and never write content through
`bash -c`, a heredoc, or `python -c` — none of those survive this shell. A file
you write is **never left empty**: an empty or half-written `src/game.rs` is a
broken candidate, and a round whose only writes were empty is recorded as a
failure.

## 2. The frozen contract, in Bevy terms

`src/contract.rs` declares and registers the seven surfaces. A new state you
want the harness to see must live in one of them (or in a new type you register
the same way), never in a private struct:

```rust
/// A marker the semantic tools address by its full path.
#[derive(Component, Reflect, Debug, Default)]
#[reflect(Component)]
pub struct Player;

/// A resource the semantic tools read by its full path.
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct CoinCounter { pub coins: i64 }

// …and registration, without which Bevy Remote Protocol answers
// `Unknown resource type` and every observation becomes a gap:
app.register_type::<Player>().register_type::<CoinCounter>();
```

Three rules that the earlier spikes paid for:

- **`#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` plus `register_type`** — a
  type that is not registered is invisible, and the adapter reports a contract
  violation rather than a zero;
- **the crate name is part of the path**: keep `name = "hof_game"` in
  `Cargo.toml` and the types in `src/contract.rs`;
- **do not hide state in an engine resource**: `bevy_time::time::Time` is not
  reflectable, which is why the game has its own `FrameCounter`.

## 3. The game's own clock

```rust
fn count_frames(mut counter: ResMut<FrameCounter>) {
    counter.frames = counter.frames.saturating_add(1);
}
```

Every observation the harness takes is stamped with this number, so it must
increment exactly once per frame.

## 4. Level-triggered input

`InputIntent` is written from outside the game
(`world.mutate_resources` on `hof_game::contract::InputIntent`), so its fields
are a **level**, not an event:

```rust
fn apply_input(
    intent: Res<InputIntent>,
    mut player: Query<(&mut Velocity, &mut Grounded, &mut JumpLatch), With<Player>>,
) {
    for (mut velocity, mut grounded, mut latch) in &mut player {
        // Held: the velocity follows the level every frame, and writing 0 stops
        // the player immediately (no inertia).
        velocity.x = MOVE_SPEED * intent.move_dir as f32;
        // Edge: the *game* consumes the press, so holding it is one jump.
        if intent.jump_pressed && grounded.on_ground && !latch.0 {
            velocity.y = JUMP_SPEED;
            grounded.on_ground = false;
        }
        latch.0 = intent.jump_pressed;
    }
}
```

Do **not** clear `move_dir` every frame: that is what made an early experiment
move 2 px where a held level moved 92 px.

## 5. A jump the harness can see

The criterion is not "the player pressed jump" but "the sampled heights rise
**and** fall, and the peak is above the take-off height". Aim for an apex about a
quarter of a second after take-off and a landing after roughly half a second:

```
rise time  ≈ JUMP_SPEED / GRAVITY      (seconds)
air time   ≈ 2 * JUMP_SPEED / GRAVITY
```

With `JUMP_SPEED = 300` and `GRAVITY = 1200` the player is airborne for ~0.5 s:
about 30 frames at 60 FPS, which the battery's sampler covers with both
directions. A jump with no gravity never falls, and a jump with no upward
impulse never rises — both are red.

## 6. Reading your own state through the tool bridge

The Developer does not need the game process to do its work (the runtime owns
the round's session and the Tester judges it), but the tools exist and their
schemas are in `.hoh/TOOLS.md`. Prefer an args file, because the shell is
`cmd.exe` on Windows:

```
%HOH_HOH_BIN% tools call bevy_coin_counter --args-file %HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR%/args/coins.json
```

Write `args/coins.json` with the write directive first (it is one line `{}`):

```text
HOH_WRITE_FILE .hoh/scratch/coins.json
{}
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE
```

and pass that path. The argument names are exactly what
`.hoh/TOOLS.md` lists — `dir` and `level` for `bevy_inject_move`, `press` for
`bevy_inject_jump`, `n` for `bevy_wait_frames`.

Reading the state of a game that was started **before you changed the code** is
not evidence about your edit; use it only to understand the tools' shapes. The
runtime owns the round's session: **do not start a game of your own** — a second
boot would replace the session the Tester is meant to reach, and the game it
started predates your edits, so it can never confirm them. Your launchability
check is `cargo build --offline`; the harness's own `play_scene_ready` step is
the boot check.

## 7. Scratch discipline

Every probe, log and temporary JSON goes under the scratch directory, which the
artifact hash ignores:

```
type %HOH_SCRATCH_DIR%\probe.json
```

Nothing may be left in the project root: no `_*`, no `tmp_*`, no `*.bak`, no
`*.tmp`, and never a second `Cargo.toml`.

## 8. When a call comes back empty

A `bevy_*` tool that answers with an empty output means the harness rejected the
request before the game saw it — almost always a missing or unreadable args
file. Write the args file first, then call:

```
%HOH_HOH_BIN% tools call bevy_health --args-file %HOH_ARTIFACT_DIR%/args/health.json
```

```
HOH_WRITE_FILE .hoh/scratch/health.json
{}
HOH_END_WRITE_FILE
```

Then read the call's own message: a contract violation names the type path that
is not registered, and a transport failure names the endpoint the runtime
published (`.hoh/PROJECT_MAP.md` and `.hoh/TOOLS.md` carry both). Do not
hand-roll JSON-RPC, do not probe ports, and do not start a second game.

1:## Project Planner Priorities
2:### Priority Order
3:1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
4:2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. [P] ## Project Planner Priorities
[P] ### Priority Order
[P] 1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
[P] 2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. Observable outcome: after injecting a move towards the coin and waiting frames, `bevy_coin_counter` returns `coins` rising from 0 to a positive integer, and the value never decreases afterwards.
[P] 3. **Reachable goal sets the one-way win flag (P3)** - Place a goal entity/marker at a spot the `Player` can actually reach along the ground (no unjumpable gap and no wall in the injected path) and add a per-frame proximity check that sets `WinFlag { won: true }`; never clear it back to false. Observable outcome: after the coin pickup, injecting a continued walk to the goal makes `bevy_win_flag` return `won == true`, and a subsequent `bevy_player_transform` sample confirms the player's x is at/near the goal position on that frame, proving the flag position is reachable rather than off-map.
[P] ### Preservation Gate
[P] - The frozen contract must not regress: crate stays `hof_game`, and `Player`, `Grounded`, `CoinCounter`, `WinFlag`, `FrameCounter`, `InputIntent` stay declared and `register_type`-ed in `src/contract.rs` with their `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` attributes and unchanged full type paths — a renamed or unregistered surface makes every readiness observation a gap, not a zero.
[P] - The observability plumbing in `src/main.rs` must not regress: `bevy_remote` feature in `Cargo.toml`, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` binding `127.0.0.1:15702`, `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode, and the `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` runtime switch — the same binary must still run windowed or windowless.
[P] - `cargo build --offline` must still exit 0 (warm rebuild against the exported `%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, no `--target-dir` override), and the headless process must stay alive for the whole round instead of exiting after one frame.
[P] - `InputIntent` must stay a level-triggered resource with named fields consumed by the game each frame (edge cleared by the game, `move_dir` never zeroed by the game) — the 2 px-versus-92 px regression must not come back.
[P] - `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` stay intact (no second manifest, no deleted lock) and no probe/scratch file is left in the project root.
[P] ### Acceptance Gate
[P] - One end-to-end driven loop against the running frozen candidate, judged through the harness's deterministic battery and the frozen contract surfaces only: (a) spawn state reads `coins == 0`, `won == false`, and `Grounded.on_ground == true`; (b) `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` then `bevy_wait_frames` shows `translation.x` advanced by tens of pixels (P1); (c) `bevy_inject_jump` plus frame waits shows sampled y rising then falling and Grounded true before take-off (P4, P5); (d) `bevy_coin_counter` reads `coins` going from 0 to a positive integer after the player reaches the coin (P2, one-way); (e) `bevy_win_flag` reads `won == true` after the player walks on to the goal, with a matching `bevy_player_transform` sample at the win frame placing the player at the reachable goal position (P3, one-way). A round is only green when (d) and (e) are both observed as well as (b)/(c); movement and jumping alone do not satisfy this gate.

extra.raw_output:
## Project Planner Priorities
### Priority Order
1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. Observable outcome: after injecting a move towards the coin and waiting frames, `bevy_coin_counter` returns `coins` rising from 0 to a positive integer, and the value never decreases afterwards.
3. **Reachable goal sets the one-way win flag (P3)** - Place a goal entity/marker at a spot the `Player` can actually reach along the ground (no unjumpable gap and no wall in the injected path) and add a per-frame proximity check that sets `WinFlag { won: true }`; never clear it back to false. Observable outcome: after the coin pickup, injecting a continued walk to the goal makes `bevy_win_flag` return `won == true`, and a subsequent `bevy_player_transform` sample confirms the player's x is at/near the goal position on that frame, proving the flag position is reachable rather than off-map.
### Preservation Gate
- The frozen contract must not regress: crate stays `hof_game`, and `Player`, `Grounded`, `CoinCounter`, `WinFlag`, `FrameCounter`, `InputIntent` stay declared and `register_type`-ed in `src/contract.rs` with their `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` attributes and unchanged full type paths — a renamed or unregistered surface makes every readiness observation a gap, not a zero.
- The observability plumbing in `src/main.rs` must not regress: `bevy_remote` feature in `Cargo.toml`, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` binding `127.0.0.1:15702`, `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode, and the `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` runtime switch — the same binary must still run windowed or windowless.
- `cargo build --offline` must still exit 0 (warm rebuild against the exported `%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, no `--target-dir` override), and the headless process must stay alive for the whole round instead of exiting after one frame.
- `InputIntent` must stay a level-triggered resource with named fields consumed by the game each frame (edge cleared by the game, `move_dir` never zeroed by the game) — the 2 px-versus-92 px regression must not come back.
- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` stay intact (no second manifest, no deleted lock) and no probe/scratch file is left in the project root.
### Acceptance Gate
- One end-to-end driven loop against the running frozen candidate, judged through the harness's deterministic battery and the frozen contract surfaces only: (a) spawn state reads `coins == 0`, `won == false`, and `Grounded.on_ground == true`; (b) `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` then `bevy_wait_frames` shows `translation.x` advanced by tens of pixels (P1); (c) `bevy_inject_jump` plus frame waits shows sampled y rising then falling and Grounded true before take-off (P4, P5); (d) `bevy_coin_counter` reads `coins` going from 0 to a positive integer after the player reaches the coin (P2, one-way); (e) `bevy_win_flag` reads `won == true` after the player walks on to the goal, with a matching `bevy_player_transform` sample at the win frame placing the player at the reachable goal position (P3, one-way). A round is only green when (d) and (e) are both observed as well as (b)/(c); movement and jumping alone do not satisfy this gate.

L1>>## Project Planner Priorities
L2>>### Priority Order
L3>>1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
L4>>2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. Observable outcome: after injecting a move towards the coin and waiting frames, `bevy_coin_counter` returns `coins` rising from 0 to a positive integer, and the value never decreases afterwards.
L5>>3. **Reachable goal sets the one-way win flag (P3)** - Place a goal entity/marker at a spot the `Player` can actually reach along the ground (no unjumpable gap and no wall in the injected path) and add a per-frame proximity check that sets `WinFlag { won: true }`; never clear it back to false. Observable outcome: after the coin pickup, injecting a continued walk to the goal makes `bevy_win_flag` return `won == true`, and a subsequent `bevy_player_transform` sample confirms the player's x is at/near the goal position on that frame, proving the flag position is reachable rather than off-map.
L6>>### Preservation Gate
L7>>- The frozen contract must not regress: crate stays `hof_game`, and `Player`, `Grounded`, `CoinCounter`, `WinFlag`, `FrameCounter`, `InputIntent` stay declared and `register_type`-ed in `src/contract.rs` with their `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` attributes and unchanged full type paths — a renamed or unregistered surface makes every readiness observation a gap, not a zero.
L8>>- The observability plumbing in `src/main.rs` must not regress: `bevy_remote` feature in `Cargo.toml`, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` binding `127.0.0.1:15702`, `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode, and the `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` runtime switch — the same binary must still run windowed or windowless.
L9>>- `cargo build --offline` must still exit 0 (warm rebuild against the exported `%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, no `--target-dir` override), and the headless process must stay alive for the whole round instead of exiting after one frame.
L10>>- `InputIntent` must stay a level-triggered resource with named fields consumed by the game each frame (edge cleared by the game, `move_dir` never zeroed by the game) — the 2 px-versus-92 px regression must not come back.
L11>>- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` stay intact (no second manifest, no deleted lock) and no probe/scratch file is left in the project root.

L13>>- One end-to-end driven loop against the running frozen candidate, judged through the harness's deterministic battery and the frozen contract surfaces only: (a) spawn state reads `coins == 0`, `won == false`, and `Grounded.on_ground == true`; (b) `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` then `bevy_wait_frames` shows `translation.x` advanced by tens of pixels (P1); (c) `bevy_inject_jump` plus frame waits shows sampled y rising then falling and Grounded true before take-off (P4, P5); (d) `bevy_coin_counter` reads `coins` going from 0 to a positive integer after the player reaches the coin (P2, one-way); (e) `bevy_win_flag` reads `won == true` after the player walks on to the goal, with a matching `bevy_player_transform` sample at the win frame placing the player at the reachable goal position (P3, one-way). ## Project Planner Priorities
### Priority Order
1. **Playable player on a ground plane (P1 + P4 + P5)** - In `src/game.rs`, spawn a `Player` entity carrying `hof_game::contract::Player` + `Transform` + `Velocity` + `Grounded` + a jump latch, plus static ground geometry, and drive it every frame from the level-triggered `InputIntent` resource (`move_dir`, `jump_pressed`) using gravity so a held `move_dir` maps to real x displacement and a press maps to an arc that rises then falls. Observable outcome: with `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` the player's `translation.x` increases by tens of pixels, `{"dir":0,"level":true}` stops it with no residual drift, `bevy_inject_jump` produces sampled `translation.y` values that both increase and decrease and land back on the ground, and `bevy_grounded` reads `on_ground == true` on the frame before take-off and `false` while airborne. `FrameCounter.frames` increments exactly once per frame throughout.
2. **Collectible coin drives the coin counter (P2)** - Place a coin entity at a position reachable by walking/jumping from the spawn point and add a per-frame contact check that sets `CoinCounter { coins }` to a positive value the first time the `Player` transform overlaps it, saturating so repeated frames over the same coin do not double-count. Observable outcome: after injecting a move towards the coin and waiting frames, `bevy_coin_counter` returns `coins` rising from 0 to a positive integer, and the value never decreases afterwards.
3. **Reachable goal sets the one-way win flag (P3)** - Place a goal entity/marker at a spot the `Player` can actually reach along the ground (no unjumpable gap and no wall in the injected path) and add a per-frame proximity check that sets `WinFlag { won: true }`; never clear it back to false. Observable outcome: after the coin pickup, injecting a continued walk to the goal makes `bevy_win_flag` return `won == true`, and a subsequent `bevy_player_transform` sample confirms the player's x is at/near the goal position on that frame, proving the flag position is reachable rather than off-map.
### Preservation Gate
- The frozen contract must not regress: crate stays `hof_game`, and `Player`, `Grounded`, `CoinCounter`, `WinFlag`, `FrameCounter`, `InputIntent` stay declared and `register_type`-ed in `src/contract.rs` with their `#[reflect(Component)]` / `#[reflect(Resource)]` attributes and unchanged full type paths — a renamed or unregistered surface makes every readiness observation a gap, not a zero.
- The observability plumbing in `src/main.rs` must not regress: `bevy_remote` feature in `Cargo.toml`, `RemotePlugin::default()` + `RemoteHttpPlugin::default()` binding `127.0.0.1:15702`, `ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(1/60)` in headless mode, and the `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` runtime switch — the same binary must still run windowed or windowless.
- `cargo build --offline` must still exit 0 (warm rebuild against the exported `%CARGO_TARGET_DIR%`, no `--target-dir` override), and the headless process must stay alive for the whole round instead of exiting after one frame.
- `InputIntent` must stay a level-triggered resource with named fields consumed by the game each frame (edge cleared by the game, `move_dir` never zeroed by the game) — the 2 px-versus-92 px regression must not come back.
- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` stay intact (no second manifest, no deleted lock) and no probe/scratch file is left in the project root.
### Acceptance Gate
- One end-to-end driven loop against the running frozen candidate, judged through the harness's deterministic battery and the frozen contract surfaces only: (a) spawn state reads `coins == 0`, `won == false`, and `Grounded.on_ground == true`; (b) `bevy_inject_move {"dir":1,"level":true}` then `bevy_wait_frames` shows `translation.x` advanced by tens of pixels (P1); (c) `bevy_inject_jump` plus frame waits shows sampled y rising then falling and Grounded true before take-off (P4, P5); (d) `bevy_coin_counter` reads `coins` going from 0 to a positive integer after the player reaches the coin (P2, one-way); (e) `bevy_win_flag` reads `won == true` after the player walks on to the goal, with a matching `bevy_player_transform` sample at the win frame placing the player at the reachable goal position (P3, one-way). A round is only green when (d) and (e) are both observed as well as (b)/(c); movement and jumping alone do not satisfy this gate.

﻿//! The game's behaviour: left/right movement, collectible coins, a reachable
//! goal, a gravity jump and the ground state that gives the jump a semantic
//! basis (PRD P1..P5).
//!
//! The numbers below are the level's design, not the contract: a Developer is
//! expected to change them (and this file) as the round's increment. Only the
//! type paths in [`crate::contract`] are frozen.
//!
//! Four properties are deliberate because the observation battery depends on
//! them:
//!
//! * **`move_dir` is a held level.** The velocity is *recomputed* from it every
//!   frame (`v = SPEED * move_dir`), so writing `0` yields exactly zero velocity
//!   and no inertia drifts (PRD P1). Clearing the intent every frame is what
//!   SPIKE-1 measured as a 2 px move over 0.4 s.
//! * **The jump's edge is consumed by the game.** `jump_pressed` is a level, so
//!   the game latches it: one press is one jump, and holding it does not bounce
//!   (the latch only re-arms when the intent goes back to `false`).
//! * **Every pickup is a real entity.** A coin is collected by the player's
//!   `Transform` actually overlapping the coin's `Transform`, and the goal is
//!   reached the same way, so the counter and the win flag are consequences of
//!   the player walking there, not of a scripted threshold.
//! * **One way only.** A collected coin is marked taken and never restored, and
//!   the win flag is only ever set to `true` -- walking back does not undo
//!   either.
//!
//! The level is deliberately *compact*: from the spawn point a single held
//! rightward walk reaches the first coin in a few frames, the second coin a
//! moment later, and the goal about 0.8 s after the key goes down, so a driven
//! sequence that only holds one direction still exercises P1, P2 and P3 end to
//! end. The ground is wider than the walk, so a drifting player cannot leave the
//! walkable plane.

use bevy::prelude::*;

use crate::contract::{CoinCounter, FrameCounter, Grounded, InputIntent, Player, WinFlag};

/// The ground plane's surface height. Also the player's starting height (the
/// player's `Transform` is at its feet, so the coin/goal boxes below are
/// expressed relative to this).
pub const GROUND_Y: f32 = -200.0;
/// How far the ground slab extends to either side of the origin. The player is
/// clamped inside this span, so the walkable plane really is finite and the
/// player can never be pushed to an x where no ground exists.
pub const GROUND_HALF_WIDTH: f32 = 1200.0;
/// The ground slab's thickness (visual / physical slab below the surface).
pub const GROUND_THICKNESS: f32 = 40.0;

/// Horizontal speed, in pixels per second. A 0.4 s hold therefore travels
/// ~80 px, which is far above the 2 px "intent was cleared" regression.
pub const MOVE_SPEED: f32 = 300.0;
/// The upwards impulse, in pixels per second.
pub const JUMP_SPEED: f32 = 420.0;
/// Downwards acceleration, in pixels per second squared. Together with
/// `JUMP_SPEED` this gives a ~0.7 s arc and a ~73 px apex: long enough that a
/// sampled `translation.y` sequence contains both rising and falling steps.
pub const GRAVITY: f32 = 1200.0;
/// The largest timestep one frame may integrate, so a slow first frame cannot
/// teleport the player past a coin or the goal.
pub const MAX_STEP_SECONDS: f32 = 1.0 / 30.0;

/// Half-width of a coin's pickup test box, in pixels.
const COIN_HALF_WIDTH: f32 = 35.0;
/// Half-width of the goal's trigger box. Narrower than the gap between the
/// second coin and the goal so the win is still reported as a distinct event,
/// but wide enough that the frame the win flag flips already has the player
/// standing inside the goal.
const GOAL_HALF_WIDTH: f32 = 25.0;
/// Half-height of both pickup test boxes, in pixels.
const PICKUP_HALF_HEIGHT: f32 = 60.0;

/// The first coin: reached ~0.15 s after a rightward hold begins.
pub const COIN_A_X: f32 = 50.0;
/// The second coin, a little further along the same walkable ground.
pub const COIN_B_X: f32 = 100.0;
/// How high a coin's centre floats above the ground surface.
pub const COIN_Y: f32 = GROUND_Y + 15.0;
/// The goal marker: on the same continuous ground, past both coins. At
/// `MOVE_SPEED` a held rightward walk touches it ~0.9 s after it begins, and
/// there is no gap, wall or jump between the spawn point and it.
pub const GOAL_X: f32 = 150.0;
/// The goal marker's centre height.
pub const GOAL_Y: f32 = GROUND_Y + 20.0;

/// The player's velocity. Private to the game; nothing observes it (the
/// contract's only position surface is the player's `Transform`).
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct Velocity {
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
}

/// The jump's own edge: `true` while `jump_pressed` is being held, so a level
/// that stays true is one jump and not a trampoline.
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct JumpLatch(bool);

/// A collectible coin. `taken` makes the pickup one-way: a coin that has been
/// collected can never be collected again, so `CoinCounter.coins` never
/// decreases.
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct Coin {
    taken: bool,
}

/// The goal marker. Reaching it sets `WinFlag.won` (one-way).
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct Goal;

/// The static ground slab reference. Nothing collides with it -- it marks where
/// the walkable surface is.
#[derive(Component, Debug, Default)]
struct GroundSlab;

pub fn add(app: &mut App) {
    app.add_systems(Startup, spawn_scene);
    // The order matters: the clock ticks first, then the intent becomes motion,
    // then the world moves, then the world's consequences are recorded.
    app.add_systems(
        Update,
        (count_frames, apply_input, integrate, collect_pickups).chain(),
    );
}

fn spawn_scene(mut commands: Commands) {
    // The static ground slab, below the surface line.
    commands.spawn((
        GroundSlab,
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, GROUND_Y - GROUND_THICKNESS * 0.5, 0.0),
    ));

    // The player: the frozen marker, an engine `Transform`, the ground state and
    // the game's own private components. It starts standing on the ground.
    commands.spawn((
        Player,
        Transform::from_xyz(0.0, GROUND_Y, 0.0),
        Grounded::default(),
        Velocity::default(),
        JumpLatch::default(),
    ));

    // Two coins on the walkable ground, ahead of the spawn point.
    commands.spawn((Coin::default(), Transform::from_xyz(COIN_A_X, COIN_Y, 0.0)));
    commands.spawn((Coin::default(), Transform::from_xyz(COIN_B_X, COIN_Y, 0.0)));

    // The goal marker, further along the same continuous ground.
    commands.spawn((Goal, Transform::from_xyz(GOAL_X, GOAL_Y, 0.0)));
}

/// The game's own clock (D297 (b)): every semantic tool reports this value as
/// `frame`, so it must advance exactly once per frame.
fn count_frames(mut counter: ResMut<FrameCounter>) {
    counter.frames = counter.frames.saturating_add(1);
}

/// Turn the held intent into velocity, and consume the jump's edge.
///
/// `move_dir` is a level: the velocity is *derived* from it, never accumulated,
/// so `0` is an immediate stop with no residual motion. The jump is an edge: the
/// latch makes a held `jump_pressed` a single take-off.
fn apply_input(
    intent: Res<InputIntent>,
    mut player: Query<(&mut Velocity, &mut Grounded, &mut JumpLatch), With<Player>>,
) {
    for (mut velocity, mut grounded, mut latch) in &mut player {
        velocity.x = MOVE_SPEED * intent.move_dir as f32;
        if intent.jump_pressed && grounded.on_ground && !latch.0 {
            velocity.y = JUMP_SPEED;
            grounded.on_ground = false;
        }
        latch.0 = intent.jump_pressed;
    }
}

/// Integrate one frame of motion and settle on the ground.
///
/// `Grounded.on_ground` is true exactly while the player's feet rest on the
/// surface: it is cleared on the take-off frame and only set again when the arc
/// comes back down, which is what the ground-state check samples before the
/// take-off.
fn integrate(
    time: Res<Time>,
    mut player: Query<(&mut Transform, &mut Velocity, &mut Grounded), With<Player>>,
) {
    let dt = time.delta_secs().min(MAX_STEP_SECONDS);
    for (mut transform, mut velocity, mut grounded) in &mut player {
        transform.translation.x = (transform.translation.x + velocity.x * dt)
            .clamp(-GROUND_HALF_WIDTH, GROUND_HALF_WIDTH);
        velocity.y -= GRAVITY * dt;
        transform.translation.y += velocity.y * dt;
        if transform.translation.y <= GROUND_Y {
            transform.translation.y = GROUND_Y;
            velocity.y = 0.0;
            grounded.on_ground = true;
        } else {
            grounded.on_ground = false;
        }
    }
}

/// The coins and the goal, resolved against the player's real position.
///
/// A coin is picked up when the player's `Transform` overlaps the coin's
/// `Transform`; the goal is reached the same way. Both are one-way: a taken coin
/// is never restored and `WinFlag.won` is only ever written `true`.
fn collect_pickups(
    mut coins: ResMut<CoinCounter>,
    mut win: ResMut<WinFlag>,
    player: Query<&Transform, With<Player>>,
    mut pickups: Query<(&Transform, Option<&mut Coin>, Option<&Goal>), Without<Player>>,
) {
    for player_transform in &player {
        let px = player_transform.translation.x;
        let py = player_transform.translation.y;

        for (pickup_transform, coin, goal) in &mut pickups {
            let dx = (px - pickup_transform.translation.x).abs();
            let dy = (py - pickup_transform.translation.y).abs();
            if dy > PICKUP_HALF_HEIGHT {
                continue;
            }

            if let Some(mut coin) = coin {
                if dx <= COIN_HALF_WIDTH && !coin.taken {
                    coin.taken = true;
                    coins.coins = coins.coins.saturating_add(1);
                }
            }

            if goal.is_some() && dx <= GOAL_HALF_WIDTH {
                win.won = true;
            }
        }
    }
}

//! The frozen reflectable contract (PRD §3-C2, DESIGN-DETAIL §3).
//!
//! Every type below is part of the observation surface: its **fully qualified
//! path including this crate's name** (`hof_game::contract::…`) is what the
//! adapter's semantic tools address, so renaming one of them is a contract
//! change, not a refactor.  Each type is declared once and registered with
//! [`register`], which `main` calls before the app runs.
//!
//! The eight surfaces:
//!
//! | surface | type | reflection |
//! |---|---|---|
//! | player marker | `Player` | `Component` |
//! | player position | `bevy_transform::components::transform::Transform` | engine-registered |
//! | ground state | `Grounded` | `Component` |
//! | coin count | `CoinCounter` | `Resource` |
//! | win flag | `WinFlag` | `Resource` |
//! | game frame counter | `FrameCounter` | `Resource` |
//! | input intent | `InputIntent` | `Resource` |
//! | process nonce | `ProcessNonce` | `Resource` |
//!
//! `Transform` is Bevy's own and is registered by the engine, so it is not
//! declared here — the adapter adds it to the contract on that basis.

use bevy::prelude::*;

/// The runtime switch that runs the same binary with no window and no GPU
/// (`PRD.md` §3-C1).  The launcher sets it; a round is **always** headless
/// (SPIKE-2 measured 4.0 FPS windowed, which is too slow to see a jump arc).
pub const HEADLESS_ENV: &str = "HOF_GAME_HEADLESS";

/// The per-launch nonce's environment variable, set by the launcher.
///
/// Readiness has to prove **which** process answered, not merely that something
/// answers: two games can both bind 15702 (Windows `SO_REUSEADDR`), and a stale
/// one answering is how round 2's battery measured the wrong artifact.  The
/// launcher generates one nonce per launch, puts it here, and the value below is
/// what it reads back off the wire.
pub const PROCESS_NONCE_ENV: &str = "HOF_GAME_PROCESS_NONCE";

/// Locates the player entity.  `world.query` filters on this path.
#[derive(Component, Reflect, Debug, Default)]
#[reflect(Component)]
pub struct Player;

/// The ground state.  Criterion ⑤ reads this *before* the take-off, so a jump
/// has a semantic basis instead of a guess from a y-coordinate.
#[derive(Component, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy)]
#[reflect(Component)]
pub struct Grounded {
    pub on_ground: bool,
}

impl Default for Grounded {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { on_ground: true }
    }
}

/// How many coins the player has collected.  `target` is informational; the
/// counter itself starts at 0 (PRD P2).
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct CoinCounter {
    pub coins: i64,
    pub target: i64,
}

impl Default for CoinCounter {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            coins: 0,
            target: 1,
        }
    }
}

/// The win flag: false until the goal is reached, and **one-way** (PRD P3).
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct WinFlag {
    pub won: bool,
}

/// The game's own frame counter (D297 (b)): incremented by the game every
/// frame.  Every value a semantic tool returns carries this number as its
/// `frame`, so a claim about "the game advanced" is a claim about the game, not
/// about how often the adapter polled.
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct FrameCounter {
    pub frames: u64,
}

/// The injection surface (PRD §3-C3).  It is a **level-triggered** resource:
/// `move_dir` stays where it was written until it is overwritten, while the
/// jump's edge is consumed by the game itself (`game::apply_input` latches
/// `jump_pressed`), so holding a direction really moves the player instead of
/// moving for a single frame.
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct InputIntent {
    pub move_dir: i32,
    pub jump_pressed: bool,
}

/// This process's launch nonce (round-2 repair).
///
/// The launcher generates one per launch and passes it in
/// [`PROCESS_NONCE_ENV`]; the value is published here so a reader can prove that
/// the process answering the endpoint is the one that launch started.  It is
/// deliberately **read-only state**: the game never derives behaviour from it,
/// and it must survive a role editing the game, because the observation path
/// depends on it.
#[derive(Resource, Reflect, Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[reflect(Resource)]
pub struct ProcessNonce {
    pub value: String,
}

impl ProcessNonce {
    /// The nonce this process was launched with, or the empty string when the
    /// game was started by hand (`cargo run`), which is not a round's launch.
    pub fn from_env() -> Self {
        Self {
            value: std::env::var(PROCESS_NONCE_ENV).unwrap_or_default(),
        }
    }
}

/// Register every game-declared surface.  The adapter's contract check reads the
/// `register_type::<…>` declarations out of this crate's source, so this
/// function is what makes the check pass.
pub fn register(app: &mut App) {
    app.register_type::<Player>()
        .register_type::<Grounded>()
        .register_type::<CoinCounter>()
        .register_type::<WinFlag>()
        .register_type::<FrameCounter>()
        .register_type::<InputIntent>()
        .register_type::<ProcessNonce>();
}

﻿//! `hof_game` 鈥?the scaffolded Bevy 0.19.1 game.
//!
//! This file is the **same binary in both modes** (PRD 搂3-C1): with
//! `HOF_GAME_HEADLESS` set it runs with no window and no render world, and
//! without it, it opens one real window.  Every round of the pipeline runs it
//! headless, because SPIKE-2 measured windowed mode at 4.0 FPS on this machine,
//! which is far too slow to observe a jump arc.
//!
//! Three facts from the spike reports are load-bearing here and must not be
//! "tidied away":
//!
//! 1. **`ScheduleRunnerPlugin` is mandatory in headless mode.**  Without it the
//!    app runs one frame and exits with code 0, and the BRP endpoint is never
//!    bound (SPIKE-2 C7).
//! 2. **`WgpuSettings { backends: None }` means "no render world at all"**, not
//!    "an empty one": Bevy never adds `ExtractPlugin`, so port 15703 does not
//!    exist.  The adapter depends on 15702 only.
//! 3. **The observation surface is declared, not inferred.**  `RemotePlugin` +
//!    `RemoteHttpPlugin` open 15702 on loopback with no authentication, which is
//!    why this build exists for development and CI only.

use std::time::Duration;

use bevy::app::ScheduleRunnerPlugin;
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::remote::{http::RemoteHttpPlugin, RemotePlugin};
use bevy::render::{settings::WgpuSettings, RenderPlugin};
use bevy::window::ExitCondition;
use bevy::winit::WinitPlugin;

mod contract;
mod game;
#[cfg(test)]
mod sim_tests;

fn main() {
    let headless = headless_requested();

    let mut window_plugin = WindowPlugin::default();
    let render_plugin = if headless {
        window_plugin.primary_window = None;
        window_plugin.exit_condition = ExitCondition::DontExit;
        window_plugin.close_when_requested = false;
        RenderPlugin {
            render_creation: WgpuSettings {
                backends: None,
                ..default()
            }
            .into(),
            ..default()
        }
    } else {
        RenderPlugin::default()
    };
    let builder = DefaultPlugins.set(window_plugin).set(render_plugin);

    let mut app = App::new();
    if headless {
        app.add_plugins(builder.build().disable::<WinitPlugin>());
        // Without this the process would run a single frame and exit.
        app.add_plugins(ScheduleRunnerPlugin::run_loop(Duration::from_secs_f64(
            1.0 / 60.0,
        )));
    } else {
        app.add_plugins(builder);
    }

    // The observation surface.  Same binary, both modes.
    app.add_plugins((RemotePlugin::default(), RemoteHttpPlugin::default()));

    app.init_resource::<contract::CoinCounter>()
        .init_resource::<contract::WinFlag>()
        .init_resource::<contract::FrameCounter>()
        .init_resource::<contract::InputIntent>()
        // Round-2 repair: the launch nonce is *this process's own* value, so it
        // is inserted rather than defaulted 鈥?`init_resource` would install the
        // empty default and every readiness check would fail.
        .insert_resource(contract::ProcessNonce::from_env());
    contract::register(&mut app);
    game::add(&mut app);

    watch_stdin();
    app.run();
}

/// The runtime switch: set (to anything but `0`) means headless.
fn headless_requested() -> bool {
    match std::env::var(contract::HEADLESS_ENV) {
        Ok(value) => value != "0",
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Exit the process when the launcher writes `quit` on stdin.
///
/// The launcher asks politely before it kills, and a game that ignored the line
/// would pay the full termination grace on every stop.  This is deliberately a
/// raw thread rather than a Bevy event: it must work in both the windowed and
/// the headless configuration, and it needs nothing from the ECS.
fn watch_stdin() {
    use std::io::BufRead;
    std::thread::spawn(|| {
        let stdin = std::io::stdin();
        for line in stdin.lock().lines() {
            match line {
                Ok(line) if line.trim() == "quit" => std::process::exit(0),
                Ok(_) => {}
                // EOF: the launcher closed the pipe without asking us to stop.
                Err(_) => break,
            }
        }
    });
}

//! Deterministic in-process simulation checks for the game's five behaviours
//! (PRD P1..P5).
//!
//! These are the Developer's self-tests, compiled only for `cargo test` and
//! never part of the shipped binary.  They drive the **real** systems declared
//! in [`crate::game`] on a bare `MinimalPlugins` app with a fixed 1/60 s
//! timestep, so the numbers they assert are the same numbers the observation
//! battery samples from the running game through the frozen contract surfaces.
//!
//! The point of each check is a *semantic* claim, not a pixel claim:
//!
//! * a held `move_dir` produces tens of pixels of displacement, and writing `0`
//!   stops the player dead (no residual velocity);
//! * a jump leaves the ground, rises, falls and lands back on the ground inside
//!   a second, and `Grounded.on_ground` is `true` before take-off and `false`
//!   while airborne;
//! * the coin counter goes 0 -> positive by walking, and never decreases;
//! * the win flag goes `false` -> `true` by walking, one-way, at a position the
//!   player actually stands at;
//! * `FrameCounter.frames` advances exactly once per `app.update()`.

#![cfg(test)]

use std::time::Duration;

use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy::time::TimeUpdateStrategy;

use crate::contract::{CoinCounter, FrameCounter, Grounded, InputIntent, Player, WinFlag};
use crate::game::{self, GROUND_Y, MOVE_SPEED};

/// The fixed timestep every observation is taken at: the headless
/// `ScheduleRunnerPlugin` runs at 60 Hz, so this mirrors the real game.
const DT: f64 = 1.0 / 60.0;

/// A fresh app with the game installed, the contract resources initialised and
/// the scene already spawned.
fn new_app() -> App {
    let mut app = App::new();
    app.add_plugins(MinimalPlugins);
    app.insert_resource(TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration(Duration::from_secs_f64(
        DT,
    )));
    app.init_resource::<CoinCounter>()
        .init_resource::<WinFlag>()
        .init_resource::<FrameCounter>()
        .init_resource::<InputIntent>();
    game::add(&mut app);
    // The first update runs `Startup`, which spawns the level.
    app.update();
    app
}

fn step(app: &mut App, frames: u32) {
    for _ in 0..frames {
        app.update();
    }
}

fn set_move(app: &mut App, dir: i32) {
    app.world_mut().resource_mut::<InputIntent>().move_dir = dir;
}

fn set_jump(app: &mut App, pressed: bool) {
    app.world_mut().resource_mut::<InputIntent>().jump_pressed = pressed;
}

fn player_pos(app: &mut App) -> Vec2 {
    let world = app.world_mut();
    let mut query = world.query_filtered::<&Transform, With<Player>>();
    let transform = query.iter(&*world).next().expect("player entity");
    Vec2::new(transform.translation.x, transform.translation.y)
}

fn on_ground(app: &mut App) -> bool {
    let world = app.world_mut();
    let mut query = world.query_filtered::<&Grounded, With<Player>>();
    query
        .iter(&*world)
        .next()
        .expect("player entity")
        .on_ground
}

fn coins(app: &mut App) -> i64 {
    app.world().resource::<CoinCounter>().coins
}

fn won(app: &mut App) -> bool {
    app.world().resource::<WinFlag>().won
}

fn frames(app: &mut App) -> u64 {
    app.world().resource::<FrameCounter>().frames
}

#[test]
fn spawn_state_is_clean() {
    let mut app = new_app();
    assert_eq!(coins(&mut app), 0, "the counter starts at 0");
    assert!(!won(&mut app), "the win flag starts false");
    assert!(on_ground(&mut app), "the player starts standing");
    assert!(player_pos(&mut app).y == GROUND_Y, "the player starts on the ground");
}

#[test]
fn frame_counter_advances_once_per_update() {
    let mut app = new_app();
    let before = frames(&mut app);
    step(&mut app, 10);
    assert_eq!(frames(&mut app), before + 10);
}

#[test]
fn held_move_dir_moves_and_zero_stops() {
    let mut app = new_app();
    let start = player_pos(&mut app).x;

    // A held direction (the level stays where it was written) must move far:
    // 30 frames at 60 Hz is 0.5 s, i.e. ~100 px at MOVE_SPEED.
    set_move(&mut app, 1);
    step(&mut app, 30);
    let travelled = player_pos(&mut app).x - start;
    assert!(
        travelled > MOVE_SPEED * 0.25,
        "a held direction should travel tens of px, got {travelled}"
    );

    // Writing 0 is an immediate stop with no residual drift.
    set_move(&mut app, 0);
    let stopped_at = player_pos(&mut app).x;
    step(&mut app, 15);
    assert!(
        (player_pos(&mut app).x - stopped_at).abs() < 0.001,
        "0 must stop the player dead, got {}",
        player_pos(&mut app).x - stopped_at
    );

    // And the intent itself is not cleared by the game (level-triggered).
    assert_eq!(app.world().resource::<InputIntent>().move_dir, 0);
    set_move(&mut app, -1);
    step(&mut app, 10);
    assert!(
        player_pos(&mut app).x < stopped_at,
        "a negative direction must move left"
    );
}

#[test]
fn jump_rises_then_lands_and_reports_ground_state() {
    let mut app = new_app();
    assert!(on_ground(&mut app), "grounded before take-off");
    let y0 = player_pos(&mut app).y;

    set_jump(&mut app, true);
    let mut apex = y0;
    let mut saw_airborne = false;
    let mut frames_airborne = 0;
    // One second of frames is enough for the whole arc.
    for _ in 0..60 {
        app.update();
        let y = player_pos(&mut app).y;
        apex = apex.max(y);
        if !on_ground(&mut app) {
            saw_airborne = true;
            frames_airborne += 1;
        }
    }
    set_jump(&mut app, false);

    assert!(saw_airborne, "the jump must clear the ground state");
    assert!(frames_airborne > 5, "the arc must last more than a few frames");
    assert!(
        apex - y0 > 20.0,
        "the jump must visibly rise, apex offset {}",
        apex - y0
    );
    assert_eq!(player_pos(&mut app).y, y0, "the jump must land back");
    assert!(on_ground(&mut app), "grounded again after landing");

    // The latch: a still-held jump does not bounce a second time.
    let landed = player_pos(&mut app).y;
    set_jump(&mut app, true);
    step(&mut app, 30);
    assert_eq!(player_pos(&mut app).y, landed, "holding jump is one jump");
    set_jump(&mut app, false);
}

#[test]
fn walking_right_collects_a_coin_and_reaches_the_goal_one_way() {
    let mut app = new_app();
    set_move(&mut app, 1);

    let mut coin_frame: Option<u64> = None;
    let mut win_frame: Option<u64> = None;
    let mut win_pos = 0.0_f32;
    let mut previous = coins(&mut app);
    let mut monotone = true;

    for frame in 0..150u64 {
        app.update();
        let now = coins(&mut app);
        if now < previous {
            monotone = false;
        }
        previous = now;
        if now > 0 && coin_frame.is_none() {
            coin_frame = Some(frame);
        }
        if won(&mut app) && win_frame.is_none() {
            win_frame = Some(frame);
            win_pos = player_pos(&mut app).x;
        }
    }
    set_move(&mut app, 0);

    let coin_frame = coin_frame.expect("a walk to the right must collect a coin");
    let win_frame = win_frame.expect("a walk to the right must reach the goal");
    assert!(monotone, "the coin counter must never decrease");
    assert!(coins(&mut app) >= 1, "the counter must end positive");
    assert!(
        coin_frame <= win_frame,
        "the coin comes before the goal on the walk"
    );
    assert!(
        win_pos > 0.0,
        "the win frame's player x must be on the goal's side, got {win_pos}"
    );

    // One-way: walking back does not undo the win, and the counter holds.
    let banked = coins(&mut app);
    set_move(&mut app, -1);
    step(&mut app, 40);
    set_move(&mut app, 0);
    assert!(won(&mut app), "the win flag is one-way");
    assert_eq!(coins(&mut app), banked, "collected coins stay collected");
}
